result: Xenon-CT in 25 CFS vs 7 controls found reduced absolute cortical blood flow in both middle cerebral artery territories in patients without psychiatric disorder and in the left MCA territory in those with one (P<0.05).
reason: Independent cohort, resting CBF by a comparable quantitative method, same direction; very small control group and no OI status.

result: Urine collected every 3 h from 0600 to 2100 showed lower free cortisol and cortisone across the day in unmedicated CFS without psychiatric comorbidity, with normal diurnal rhythm, while cortisol metabolites and metabolite ratios did not differ.
reason: Urinary free cortisol is one of the finding's measures; same direction in a medication-free cohort, though metabolites were not lower.

result: In a population-based sample (43 CFS vs 53 controls, CANTAB), only CFS patients with high mental fatigue had impaired spatial working memory and sustained attention, with attention declining late in the task; low-mental-fatigue patients performed like controls.
reason: Same measures (working memory, sustained attention); adds a subgroup defined by mental fatigue and within-test cognitive fatigability.

result: Generalised joint hypermobility was present in 20.6% of 68 adult CFS patients vs 4.3% of 69 matched controls, most patients met benign joint hypermobility syndrome criteria, and hypermobility was not associated with musculoskeletal pain.
reason: Independent adult case-control cohort, same measure (Beighton-based hypermobility), same direction.

result: Quantitative flow cytometry found significantly lower intracellular perforin in NK cells of CFS patients than controls, with a trend to lower perforin in cytotoxic T cells.
reason: Gives a molecular mechanism (perforin content) for reduced NK cytotoxicity; cytotoxicity itself was not measured, and Theorell 2017 found no granule-content difference.

result: In a population-based Wichita sample (58 CFS vs 55 controls), head-up tilt showed orthostatic instability in 30% of CFS (all POTS) vs 48% of controls; stand tests were negative in everyone and severity was not associated with tilt results.
reason: A 30% POTS rate falls inside the finding's 6-43% range, so it does not contradict it; it adds population-based controls with similar rates, which questions specificity.

result: In 31 CFS vs 31 healthy, 15 depressed and 22 rheumatoid arthritis controls, none of the previously reported urinary amino-acid or organic-acid abnormalities (CFSUM1/CFSUM2) were confirmed; the authors report unquantified hints of inflammation and reduced intramuscular collagen.
reason: Mainly urinary targeted analytes; it does not test blood-metabolome effect sizes or classification, and the collagen claim is too vague to link to omics-collagen-metso.

result: Radioenzymatic assay showed no differences in plasma or urinary total, free or acyl carnitine, or in their renal excretion, between 31 UK CFS patients and healthy, depressed and rheumatoid arthritis controls.
reason: Tests the same plasma free/acyl carnitine measure and finds no difference; small sample may miss a -0.2 SD effect.

result: After a maximal exercise test, self-observed fatigue in 20 CFS patients stayed raised for up to 2 days, while in 20 controls it returned to baseline within 2 h; actometer-measured activity did not fall in either group.
reason: Independent cohort showing prolonged post-exertional fatigue compared with controls; small and self-report based, and the 2-day duration is shorter than the finding's.

result: 20 CFS-only patients had baseline deficits in processing speed, consistency and efficiency vs 26 sedentary controls, while 19 CFS+FM patients did not; 25 min of cycling at 40% peak VO2 neither worsened nor improved cognition in any group.
reason: Same measures and replicates the deficit; adds FM-comorbidity heterogeneity, and the null after light exercise qualifies the finding's claim that cognition worsens after exertion.
